summary.headline: Leela Palaces Q1 FY27: operating revenue up 28% to INR3,520 mn and operating EBITDA up 41% to INR1,434 mn, margin 41%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was driven by domestic demand, which offset a weak international start to the quarter caused by West Asia travel disruption. Six owned hotels (including Coorg) posted occupancy of 67.5% (vs 63.6%), RevPAR up 17% and ADR up 10%, with same-store RevPAR up 15%. Operating EBITDA margin expanded 383 bps to 41%, and consolidated PAT rose five-fold to INR488 mn despite a INR156 mn share-of-loss from the Dubai JV. Management reiterated double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: ~5x YoY; after INR156 mn share of JV loss (Dubai)

financial_highlights.value: 1.6x (gross debt ~INR1,600 crore, net debt INR1,332 crore)

segments.name: City hotels
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 14% YoY. Bengaluru and Chennai are GDS and corporate heavy; Delhi and Jaipur called out as strong performers.

segments.name: Resorts
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 24% YoY, with high double-digit occupancy and ADR growth at the two Rajasthan resorts; Coorg acquired and rebranded as The Leela Coorg Forest Sanctuary on 8 July, reached EBITDA break-even in the quarter.

segments.name: Dubai JV (25% stake, Brookfield sponsor)
segments.commentary: Operationally break-even but recorded an accounting loss at SPV level (interest and depreciation), flowing through as INR156 mn share of JV loss. Leela takes over operations in CY27, followed by about a year of renovation.

segments.name: HMA / managed portfolio
segments.commentary: HMA fees INR262 mn (+86%); other operational service revenue +26%. Management said fees are partly performance-linked and key-money-linked, so quarterly growth may vary.

guidance_outlook: FY27: reiterated double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens operating EBITDA growth.
Second half expected to be strong as international arrivals, incentives and conferences return; Oct-Mar cited as the peak international months.
Operating EBITDA margin expected to hold near Q1 levels (~41%) or grow marginally QoQ; management cites ~50% annual margin.
Srinagar and Bandhavgarh resorts expected Oct-Dec 2027; Jaisalmer and Leela Residences Mumbai on track for FY27 year-end; Agra, Ayodhya, Sikkim and Ranthambore in CY28; Tadoba in CY30.
FY30 target of INR20 bn EBITDA reiterated; ROCE to move from double-digit to mid-to-high teens over the coming years as new hotels stabilise.
Leverage comfort level of around 2.5x average net debt/EBITDA, with variation across quarters.
capex_capacity: Portfolio at 25 properties, 5,257 keys: 15 operational hotels and 10 in pipeline; roughly half of keys owned and half managed.
Tadoba (Maharashtra) concession signed with MTDC: 30 luxury keys on 62 acres, INR1,200 mn project, 60-year concession extendable by 30 years, targeted CY30; management cites 15-17% yield on cost.
Ranthambore: 400-year-old fortress wall stabilisation has delayed the project by about two quarters; management expects to catch up once complete.
Mumbai Residences: 63 keys; show-arounds from end-CY26, residents expected early CY27.

Bandhavgarh villa construction started; Srinagar walling and landscaping in progress; Agra piling under way; Ayodhya main piling to start mid-to-late August after test piling; Sikkim main block civil work started.
Coorg 19-key brownfield expansion to follow stabilisation of the operating asset.
Renewable energy share about 67%, targeted at 75%; renewable project planned at Coorg and Chennai to reduce fixed costs.
demand_pricing: International room revenue at the five owned palace hotels moved from a 10% YoY decline in March to a 1% YoY increase in June.
Domestic room revenue up 25% YoY at the five palace hotels; retail segment up more than 20%.
Leela website share of bookings is 16% (about 64% direct overall); management says direct acquisition costs about one-third of OTA cost.
Management said the international/domestic mix is roughly 50:50 and expects international to recover further in H2 FY27.
Occupancy of existing five palace hotels close to 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Are occupancies on track for mid-70s in FY27, given Q1 occupancy of 67%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an FY occupancy target. It pointed to balanced growth across city hotels (+14%) and resorts (+24%), and expects H2 international demand to add compression.

qa_highlights.question: Tadoba: underwritten ARR, occupancy and IRR? Could it open before CY30? Leverage cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tadoba is a value-accretive deal with 15-17% yield on cost, and the timeline reflects approvals and design for a wildlife trail. Net debt/LTM EBITDA is 1.6x, with an average comfort level of 2.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion timelines: have Bandhavgarh, Srinagar, Ayodhya and Agra slipped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slippage is about one quarter. Srinagar and Bandhavgarh are for CY27 (Oct-Dec for the latter), Jaisalmer and Leela Residences by year-end, and Ranthambore is delayed by about two quarters due to wall stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the HMA fee growth sustainable (run-rate around INR100 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HMA fees depend on performance, key-money-linked structures and ramp-up of new hotels, so quarterly growth will vary, but the trajectory is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 24% resort RevPAR growth beyond base effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to FIT share gains, repositioning (kids clubs, F&B, spa, Amber Terrace), and multi-generational and drive-to demand, with high double-digit growth in both Rajasthan resorts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainability of the EBITDA margin, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited renegotiated AMC and central procurement rates, revenue growth and renewable energy share. It guided to around 41% for the summer quarter, with about 50% for the full year.

risks_watch: International demand recovery: international room revenue at five palace hotels moved from -10% YoY in March to +1% in June; management expects H2 (Oct-Mar) to add compression, but West Asia conflict is not fully normalised.

Dubai JV: SPV accounting loss (asset-level interest and depreciation) drove a INR156 mn share-of-loss; Leela takes over operations in CY27 followed by about a year of renovation; residence sale plan assumes 2-3 years.

Timeline slippage: Ranthambore delayed about two quarters by fortress wall stabilisation; management says other projects slipped about one quarter and expects catch-up. Srinagar and Bandhavgarh now Oct-Dec 2027.
HMA fee sustainability: fees are partly performance-linked and key-money-linked, and management declined to give a run-rate; quarterly growth may vary.
Margin durability: Q1 41% is a summer-quarter margin versus about 50% for the full year per management; guided to hold near 41% or grow marginally QoQ. Coorg is still ramping.
Leverage: net debt/LTM EBITDA 1.6x; management comfort level averages 2.5x, with variation across quarters, and debt-funded capex and acquisitions are contemplated.
key_quotes: And we re-iterate that based on the current operating environment and the momentum that we are seeing in our business, we remain very confident on delivering double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for FY27.
So HMA is an ongoing business for us. The HMA contracts have various fee structures, incentive linked to performance and past key money commitments.
And you are right, that's got delayed by a couple of quarters, but we have now stabilized the wall and this is work in progress, but this is a one-time activity when we are building in Ranthambore.
Plus our renewable share of energy is around 67%, which we intend to take it to 75%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 guidance and on domestic demand, reiterating double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth with no headwinds foreseen. Cautious and non-committal on specifics: no FY occupancy target, no HMA run-rate, no Tadoba IRR/ARR, and BRICS pricing details withheld for sensitivity reasons.

adds.what: Coorg resort (19-key brownfield expansion to follow stabilisation; acquired and rebranded Leela Coorg Forest Sanctuary, live)
Srinagar and Bandhavgarh resorts, opening Oct-Dec 2027
Jaisalmer hotel and Leela Residences Mumbai (63 keys), on track for FY27 year-end; Mumbai residents expected early CY27
Tadoba concession, 30 luxury keys, INR1,200 mn project, targeted CY30
Agra, Ayodhya, Sikkim and Ranthambore hotels, targeted CY28 (Ranthambore delayed about two quarters)

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth, backed by Q1 RevPAR +17% and occupancy at 67.5%, a strong H2 international recovery outlook, and new hotels (Srinagar, Bandhavgarh, Jaisalmer, Mumbai Residences) due through FY27 year-end, though no order-book or quantified pipeline numbers for FY27 growth were given.
